# Crash report

### What happened?

A JIT build with the patch below applied will frequently segfault. A way to reproduce is to start an interpreter (with PyREPL) and hold the space key.

The necessary patch:
```diff
diff --git a/Include/internal/pycore_backoff.h b/Include/internal/pycore_backoff.h
index fadd11f04ec..3e779a141af 100644
--- a/Include/internal/pycore_backoff.h
+++ b/Include/internal/pycore_backoff.h
@@ -125,7 +125,7 @@ trigger_backoff_counter(void)
 // For example, 4095 does not work for the nqueens benchmark on pyperformance
 // as we always end up tracing the loop iteration's
 // exhaustion iteration. Which aborts our current tracer.
-#define JUMP_BACKWARD_INITIAL_VALUE 4000
+#define JUMP_BACKWARD_INITIAL_VALUE 63
 #define JUMP_BACKWARD_INITIAL_BACKOFF 6
 static inline _Py_BackoffCounter
 initial_jump_backoff_counter(_PyPolicy *policy)
@@ -139,7 +139,7 @@ initial_jump_backoff_counter(_PyPolicy *policy)
  * Must be larger than ADAPTIVE_COOLDOWN_VALUE,
  * otherwise when a side exit warms up we may construct
  * a new trace before the Tier 1 code has properly re-specialized. */
-#define SIDE_EXIT_INITIAL_VALUE 4000
+#define SIDE_EXIT_INITIAL_VALUE 63
 #define SIDE_EXIT_INITIAL_BACKOFF 6

 static inline _Py_BackoffCounter
diff --git a/Include/internal/pycore_uop.h b/Include/internal/pycore_uop.h
index e828a1cc5a5..538bd3bc630 100644
--- a/Include/internal/pycore_uop.h
+++ b/Include/internal/pycore_uop.h
@@ -38,9 +38,9 @@ typedef struct _PyUOpInstruction{
 // This is the length of the trace we translate initially.
 #ifdef Py_DEBUG
     // With asserts, the stencils are a lot larger
-#define UOP_MAX_TRACE_LENGTH 2000
+#define UOP_MAX_TRACE_LENGTH 8000
 #else
-#define UOP_MAX_TRACE_LENGTH 5000
+#define UOP_MAX_TRACE_LENGTH 8000
 #endif
 #define UOP_BUFFER_SIZE (UOP_MAX_TRACE_LENGTH * sizeof(_PyUOpInstruction))
 
```

### Comment 2 — devdanzin, 2026-01-12T21:21:58Z

Source: [https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143751#issuecomment-3740539753](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143751#issuecomment-3740539753)

````text
It's the actual JIT:
```
CC=clang-21 ./configure --enable-experimental-jit --with-pydebug --with-address-sanitizer --without-pymalloc
```
````

### Comment 3 — Fidget-Spinner, 2026-01-12T21:35:31Z

Source: [https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143751#issuecomment-3740582981](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143751#issuecomment-3740582981)

```text
So I'm not too sure whether to accept this issue, as we explicitly limit the trace length because our counters have limits (e.g. the JIT itself is limited to 2MB jitted size).

I will investigate further to see if it's hitting a limit, or an actual issue is happening.
```

### Comment 4 — Fidget-Spinner, 2026-01-12T22:06:59Z

Source: [https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143751#issuecomment-3740738822](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143751#issuecomment-3740738822)

```text
Ok yeah this is a generated code limit I think. I can't reproduce this with just the tier 2 interpreter, so that means it's a machine code problem.
```
